subject: MSA / Order Form redlines — liability caps, SLA credits relationship
messages:
From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@beaconpay.com>

Cc: contracts@beaconpay.com, oliver.park@beaconpay.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA & Order Form — redlines attached

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Attached are Beacon's redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. High level flags we want to call out so legal can see them quickly:

- Limitation of liability: Beacon prefers a cap equal to fees paid in the prior 12 months (not multiple of fees).
- Consequential damages: standard mutual exclusion requested.
- SLA / service credits: Beacon treats service credits as the sole and exclusive remedy for SLA breaches — and wants that reflected in Section 6 (Sole Remedy).
- Carve-outs: Beacon will accept carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct but is pushing back on broad IP/data breach carve-outs that would subvert the cap.

See attached PDF (Beacon_redlines_MSA.pdf) and the Order Form Word doc with line edits.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can accept credits-as-sole-remedy (and whether we can keep caps that exclude security/data breach)?

Thanks,
Sophie Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
Beacon Payments

Attachments: Beacon_redlines_MSA.pdf (pdf), Beacon_orderform_redline.docx (docx)

Appreciate the clear redlines and the summary. Looping in Rishi (legal) and Laura (AM lead) to review. Quick points from a commercial/sales perspective:

- Credits-as-sole-remedy for SLA is something we can consider, but we typically insist on carve-outs (IP infringement, data breaches, willful misconduct) where cap doesn't apply.
- We usually have a liability cap tied to fees but with floor minimums for larger contracts — Ill leave the exact language to Rishi.

Rishi / Laura: can you review Beacon's edits and share a counter that preserves our operational protections (particularly: ability to exclude security breaches from an overall cap; clarify relationship between credits and direct damages).

I'll stay on the thread to keep Beacon updated.

Marissa / Laura / Sophie —

Thanks for the ping. Quick legal read and proposed approach below (high level):

1) Liability cap: propose primary cap of the greater of (i) USD $2,000,000 or (ii) three (3) times the fees paid under the Order Form in the prior 12 months. That gives us a predictable ceiling while giving Beacon comfort on a fees-tied cap.

2) Carve-outs from cap: we should preserve carve-outs for (a) bodily injury/physical damage (not likely here), (b) willful misconduct, (c) gross negligence, (d) IP infringement claims, and (e) breaches of confidentiality/security (data breaches). These are standard and important for our risk posture.

3) Consequential damages: mutual exclusion remains standard. Keep the broad exclusion but ensure it doesn't swallow direct damages.

4) SLA credits / sole remedy: Beacon's request that service credits be the "sole and exclusive remedy" for SLA breaches is accepted sometimes by vendors, but we need express language that: (a) credits are the sole remedy ONLY for SLA performance failures, (b) credits do not limit Beacon's rights for data breaches, IP claims, or willful misconduct, and (c) credits themselves should be subject to a cap (e.g., credits payable in any 12-month period not to exceed 12 months of fees for the affected service).

5) Drafting note: do NOT include language that converts credits into a de facto reduction of the liability cap unless we explicitly permit an offset. Instead, keep credits separate and state whether credits are recoverable in addition to damages in carve-out scenarios.

I'm attaching a short redline with suggested language snippets (redline_suggestions.docx). If Beacon insists on credits-as-sole-remedy without carve-outs, we'll need a commercial concession (higher liability cap / security SLA escalation, or indemnity enhancements).

Happy to prepare a clean MSA redline for signature if we agree on the positions above.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_suggestions.docx

From: contracts@beaconpay.com

Subject: Beacon counterproposal on Liability / SLA credits

Marissa / Rishi,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from Beacon legal based on Rishi's points:

- Beacon's preferred liability cap remains fees paid in prior 12 months. We cannot accept a fixed-dollar floor (e.g., $2M) without additional commercial consideration.
- Regarding carve-outs: Beacon will accept carve-outs for fraud and willful misconduct, but insists that data breach claims be governed by the security/data obligations and remedies section rather than an automatic carve-out from the cap.
- On SLA credits: Beacon's position is that credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for performance shortfalls described in the SLA. They are prepared to cap total credits at 12 months of fees but want explicit exclusivity language.

If Redwood can move the cap to fees-in-prior-12-months (no floor) and accept credits-as-sole-remedy (with the 12-month credit cap), Beacon can sign quickly.

Please see attached high-level counter (beacon_counterproposals.pdf).

Best,
Beacon Payments Legal
contracts@beaconpay.com

Attachments: beacon_counterproposals.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: contracts@beaconpay.com, sophie.chen@beaconpay.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beacon counterproposal on Liability / SLA credits

Thanks for the clear stance. To move this forward commercially, Redwood can offer the following compromise proposal for the MSA/Order Form:

- Liability cap: greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (ii) USD $1,500,000. (This is a concession on our $2M floor; it balances their ask while protecting Redwood.)
- Carve-outs: explicit carve-outs for willful misconduct, gross negligence, and IP infringement. For data/security incidents, we propose remedies to live in the security section and an exception that lets data breach claims proceed beyond the cap if they arise from a Redwood breach of its obligations (we are not proposing unlimited exposure but a clear process for security remediation and additional remedies in that scenario).
- SLA credits: accept credits-as-sole-remedy for SLA failures in the SLA section, BUT credits will be capped at 12 months of fees for the impacted service and will not bar recovery for claims that fall within the carve-outs above (IP, willful misconduct, data breach as described).

If Beacon can accept the above compromise, Rishi will produce a clean MSA redline and we can circulate a DocuSign for execution.

Marissa
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Final draft language and request to proceed to redline

Beacon / Sophie —

Per Marissa's commercial compromise, here's draft MSA language I will put into a clean redline if you agree:

"Section 6. Limitation of Liability. Except for liability arising from (a) fraud, (b) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (c) infringement of a party's intellectual property rights, and (d) breach of the parties' confidentiality or security obligations, each party's aggregate liability for all claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees actually paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, or (ii) USD $1,500,000."

"Section 7. Service Level Credits; Exclusive Remedy for SLA. If Redwood fails to meet the Service Levels set forth in an applicable SLA, Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for such failure shall be the service credits set forth in the SLA. Total service credits payable to Customer for SLA breaches shall not exceed an amount equal to twelve (12) months of fees for the affected service; provided, however, that the foregoing shall not limit Customer's rights to seek damages arising from claims that are within the carve-outs set forth in Section 6 (including claims arising from Redwood's breach of its security obligations or willful misconduct)."

If Beacon accepts the compromise wording above, I'll circulate the clean tracked redline (MSA + Order Form) and include the DocuSign envelope. If Beacon cannot accept the $1.5M floor we proposed, we will need a further commercial concession (e.g., extended onboarding credits, higher SLA credits, or increased fees).

Please confirm and I'll push the MSA redline this afternoon.

-Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
